exposure: country income level (High-Income Countries vs. Low- and Middle-Income Countries)
outcome: number of caesarean sections performed annually by participants
incidence of major complications or mortality during training
cohort: A total of 411 participants from 42 countries, primarily specialists and trainees in obstetrics and gynecology, were included in the study.
finding: The study revealed significant differences in caesarean section training practices between LMIC and HIC, with LMIC participants performing more CS but completing fewer supervised cases and reporting a higher incidence of major complications or mortality during training.
mod_finding: Participants from LMIC performed more caesarean sections annually (mean 138) compared to HIC participants (mean 44), yet they completed fewer supervised cases (median 10 vs. 50) and reported a higher incidence of major complications or mortality during training (11% vs. 3%).
country: 42 countries (global comparison between High-Income and Low- and Middle-Income Countries)
cross-section timing: Current practices at the time of the survey distribution
